Performers
Magda Tagliaferro (piano), Orchestre des Concerts Lamoureux (orchestra), Jean Fournet (conductor) Documented

Named in the Commons description of this file and of the two other movements of the same performance. MusicWeb International’s review of the APR set of Tagliaferro’s 78-rpm recordings names the 1954 Concerto No. 5 with the Orchestre Lamoureux under Jean Fournet, and Discogs lists the Philips LP with the same performers. Individual orchestral players are not identified.

[1] [4] [5]
Work version
Second movement of the concerto for piano and orchestra, composed in Egypt in spring 1896; complete movement Documented

Commons describes the file as a complete piece for piano and orchestra. The orchestral edition used is not stated.

[1] [3]
Recorded
1954 Documented

Commons gives the first recording date as 1954. The day and month are not stated. The file’s 2021 date is the upload date.

[1]
Place
Salle Apollo, Paris Documented

Place of recording as stated in the Commons description; MusicWeb’s review of APR 7312 gives Salle Apollo, Paris, 1954 for the Philips recording.

[1] [4]
Label
Philips Inferred, not documented

MusicWeb International’s review of APR 7312 lists the Salle Apollo recording of 1954 as a Philips recording, and Discogs lists the concerto on Philips. The Commons description itself credits a library collection and names no label.

[4] [5]
Catalogue
Philips N 00664 R (10-inch LP, Netherlands, 1954) Inferred, not documented

Discogs gives this issue as the concerto by the same performers, Andante split across the two sides (“Andante” and “Andante (Concl.)”). Whether the Médiathèque’s file was transferred from this issue is not stated.

[5]
Matrix, take, sides
Unknown Unknown

No matrix, take or side information is given. The three movements are separate files on Commons.

[1]
Transfer
Médiathèque Musicale Mahler, Paris 8e Documented

Named as the source in the Commons description; an individual transfer engineer is not identified.

[1]
Transfer date
Unknown Unknown

The Commons date field (14 August 2021) is the upload date, not a transfer date.

[1]
Processing
Unknown Unknown

No restoration, equalisation or speed correction is described.

[1]
Composition rights
Public domain: Saint-⁠Saëns died on 16 December 1921 Documented

Commons tags the composition PD-old-70-1923. This is separate from the sound recording.

[1] [6]
Recording rights
Territorial — Commons tag PD-EU-audio for a 1954 recording Inferred, not documented

The tag asserts publication in the European Union more than 70 years ago with performers’ and producers’ rights expired. The Commons description gives the recording year, 1954; Discogs dates the Dutch Philips LP of the concerto to 1954, which supports first publication in the EU before 1956. US status is not established.
